오늘 챙겨야 할 해외 이슈

1미국 7월 PCE 물가지표 발표와 연준 금리 인상 확률 상승 7월 근원 PCE가 전년 대비 3.7%로 전월과 동일하게 유지되고 월간 기준 0.2% 상승하면서, 시장이 9월 FOMC에서 25bp 인상 확률을 40% 이상으로 반영하기 시작했습니다. 연준 인사들이 인플레이션 지속 시 추가 인상이 필요하다고 발언한 점과 맞물려, 달러 인덱스가 0.24% 상승하고 유로화가 약세를 보이는 등 통화정책 기대 변화가 외환 및 채권 시장의 단기 변동성을 키울 수 있어 지켜봐야 합니다. 2 잭슨홀 심포지엄을 앞둔 연준 의장 발언과 통화정책 기조 전환 가능성 파월 의장이 무역 정책과 글로벌 성장 둔화를 하방 리스크로 지목하며 연준이 성장을 뒷받침하기 위해 행동할 준비가 됐다고 언급했고, 시장은 7월 금리 인하를 선반영하며 2년물 국채 금리 하락과 달러 약세로 반응했습니다. 이번 주 잭슨홀 회의에서 연준이 인플레이션 데이터 강세와 성장 리스크 사이에서 어떤 신호를 보낼지가 채권 금리 곡선과 달러 방향성, 위험자산 심리에 직접적인 영향을 줄 전망입니다. 3 이란 제재 강화와 미중 정상회담을 둘러싼 지정학적 긴장 고조 미국이 이란 관련 단체 60여 곳과 중국 관련 기업을 제재 대상에 포함시켰으나, 시장은 이를 즉각적 공급 차질로 받아들이지 않고 유가와 금리가 소폭 하락하는 데 그쳤습니다. 트럼프-시진핑 정상회담을 앞두고 중국이 이란 원유 수입을 부분적으로 줄이는 선에서 협조할 가능성이 거론되는 만큼, 중동 리스크가 에너지 가격과 글로벌 교역 흐름에 미칠 파급력을 예의주시할 필요가 있습니다. 4 IMF의 글로벌 성장 전망 하향과 재정·에너지·AI 복합 리스크 경고 게오르기에바 총재가 세계 경제가 이란발 에너지 충격을 예상보다 잘 견뎠으나, 높은 부채와 지속적인 인플레이션, AI 투자 확대에 따른 수요 충격이 맞물려 하방 리스크가 우세하다고 평가했습니다. 2026년 성장 전망치를 3.0%로 낮춘 가운데, 유가 재상승 시 인플레이션 압력 재점화와 재정 악화, 금리 인상 장기화 가능성이 동시에 거론되고 있어 거시 환경의 구조적 변화를 모니터링해야 합니다. 5 비트코인 8만 달러 돌파와 달러 디베이스먼트 논쟁 재점화 미국 재무부의 유동성 공급 프로그램에 대한 우려가 완화되지 않은 가운데, 비트코인이 8만 달러를 넘어서는 등 암호화폐 시장이 강세를 보이며 '달러 가치 하락' 베팅이 재부상하고 있습니다. 금 가격이 고점 부근에서 유지되고 독일 10년물 금리가 3.22%대에서 높은 수준을 지속하는 점과 함께, 대체 자산으로의 자금 흐름이 달러와 미 국채 수급에 미치는 영향을 살펴볼 시점입니다.

Dollar Holds in Narrow Range Ahead of Key Inflation Data, Jackson Hole
www.globalbankingandfinance.com · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

The US dollar rose after a batch of stronger-than-expected inflation data and higher rate-hike expectations from the Federal Reserve. Key points: - PCE inflation for July rose 3.7% YoY (unchanged from June) and month-over-month PCE +0.2%, nudging markets to price in a ~40%+ chance of a 25 bps Fed rate hike at the September meeting. - The dollar index climbed about 0.24%, with the euro weaker; currency moves reflected rising expectations for tighter US policy. - Fed officials highlighted the need to raise rates if inflation remains too high, reinforcing hawkish expectations. - ECB signals: policymakers view further rate hikes as likely to contain inflation amid geopolitical and euro-zone strength, contributing to diverging FX dynamics. - Market context: prior concerns about dollar debasement from a Treasury liquidity program eased somewhat, but longer-dated debt moves remain in focus. Bottom line: Stronger US inflation data lifted Fed rate-hike expectations, supporting a firmer dollar; geopolitical risks and central-bank tightening rhetoric (especially from the ECB) continue to shape global macro and equity/FX markets.

US Fed chief says trade and global growth remain big risk factors | Al Jazeera Mirror
Reuters · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - Fed Chair Jerome Powell warned that trade policy and a weak global economy remain important downside risks to the US expansion, and the Fed is prepared to act to sustain growth. - Prepared remarks suggest markets expect a rate cut later in July, with futures pricing in a meaningful cut; two-year Treasuries fell and the dollar weakened as investors moved toward easing expectations. - Powell highlighted that Trump-era trade tensions, especially with China and Mexico, and heightened policy uncertainty are weighing on investment and global trade, reinforcing calls for rate reductions. - Despite solid US job growth, uncertainty about tariffs and global demand has shifted the focus from trade as a sideshow to a central macro risk for growth and capex. - Fed staff assessments indicate rising tariffs likely had a material impact on global trade last year, contributing to slower investment and capex plans amid policy uncertainty.

IMF's Georgieva says global economy weathering energy shock, sees fiscal concerns

Summary: - IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva says the global economy has weathered the energy shock from the Iran war better than feared, but warns about growing fiscal pressures and higher borrowing costs. - Growth risks look balanced but tilted to the downside due to high debt, persistent inflation, and potential AI-driven demand shifts; central banks may need to stay restrictive to control inflation. - The energy shock is not over: a renewed oil-price rise could spike inflation and force tighter policy, impacting debt service and activity. - She highlighted a “tug of war” between negative energy supply shocks and growth from AI investment, with effects spreading beyond the US. - Countries should address fiscal deficits and debt trajectories, and pursue credible consolidation plans. She urged central banks to remain laser-focused on price stability. - IMF is refining its assessments of external imbalances and trade/industrial policy interactions; no new global growth forecast was issued beyond the July projection of 3.0% for 2026. - She did not name specific countries, but has previously urged China to rebalance growth toward domestic demand to reduce global imbalances and trade tensions. Trump's trade truce with China faces test with Iran effort | AP News
apnews.com · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - The U.S. is expanding an “economic outline” to pressure Iran, targeting Iran-linked entities and several China-related actors, while China remains Iran’s top trading partner and major oil customer. - With a Trump-Xi summit looming, Washington aims to pressure Iran without provoking a broader US-China clash that could hurt the economy. Key question: how hard the U.S. can press China without triggering escalation before the Xi visit. - China signals limited cooperation: Beijing stresses compliance with international law and hints it may cut back Iran oil imports without severing ties entirely, to avoid undermining its own interests. - Observers caution that China won’t back Iran to the point of economic collapse; a targeted approach (not complete divestment) is seen as more likely to secure concessions on issues like Iran’s influence around the Strait of Hormuz. - The Treasury is sanctioning roughly 60 Iran-linked entities, including a China-owned tanker and a Hong Kong company, highlighting continued U.S. pressure on Iran despite the China angle. - Analysts suggest Trump is unlikely to ramp up tension with China ahead of Xi’s visit, as both sides seek a stable, if limited, trade détente; a broader backlash before the November summit remains a risk. Relevance to user query: - Global macro implications: The Iran-focused sanctions campaign intersects with U.S.-China dynamics, potentially affecting global energy flows and financial systems. - Stock market and Fed context: The cautious approach around China ahead of Xi’s visit suggests tempered risk of sharp policy missteps; a stable U.S.-China tone may support markets, while sanctions on Iran keep oil/international risk in play. - Geopolitical risk: The balance between pressuring Iran and preserving China relations is a key swing factor for geopolitical risk in the near term.

Wall Street Slides as Iran Diplomacy and US Inflation Data Set Up an 'Economic D-Day' Week
market.news · 2026-08-25T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: Wall Street opened lower ahead of an “economic D-Day” week that pits Iran nuclear diplomacy against key US inflation data. The dual-risk setup—potential Iran breakthrough or breakdown plus the US core PCE inflation print—is driving a cautious, risk-off tone across markets. A diplomatic breakthrough could ease oil prices, inflation, and Fed rate pressures, boosting equities and bonds; a breakdown could push crude higher, lift inflation expectations, and pressure equities—especially rate-sensitive groups—while potentially boosting defense names. The week’s outcome hinges on: US core PCE timing, Iran talks signals, and Fed commentary. International markets (Singapore, Hong Kong, India) are reacting to this sentiment overnight. Key takeaways: - Energy stocks diverge: oil majors gain on breakdown risk yet a breakthrough would ease crude. - Fed rate expectations shift with the inflation print. - Defense sector may benefit from heightened geopolitical risk. - Monitor: US core PCE, Iran communiqués, and Fed commentary to gauge weekly direction.

Global Economy Weathered Oil Shock Better Than Feared: IMF
hdfcsky.com · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

IMF Chief Kristalina Georgieva says the global economy has weathered the oil shock from the Strait of Hormuz better than feared, helped by oil/gas drawdowns, higher non-Gulf supplies, and a strong AI investment boom (notably in the US). She describes a tug-of-war between negative supply shocks from West Asia and positive demand shocks from AI, with net effects varying by country’s energy exposure, macro vulnerabilities, and AI position. Risks remain tilted to the downside, including potential renewed oil price pressures, rising fiscal strains, and slower disinflation. For low-income and oil-importing economies, energy/commodity disruptions could threaten growth and food security, and the AI gap could widen development disparities. IMF’s global growth forecast was cut to 3% for 2026, with a mid-October update due at the IMF-WB meetings. Implications for markets: ongoing uncertainty around inflation, energy prices, and the AI-driven demand boost, with potential spillovers to debt service and policy rates.

Global economy's next big threat? IMF flags Iran war, inflation and AI risks
www.moneycontrol.com · 2026-08-25T19:46:13.000Z

IMF Chief Kristalina Georgieva warns the global economy faces a tug-of-war between negative supply shocks from the Middle East (Iran war, higher energy costs) and positive demand from AI investment. Key takeaways: - Elevated borrowing costs, higher bond yields, and sticky inflation limit policy room; central banks should stay focused on inflation. - Global debt levels and budget gaps could worsen if financing remains costly. - Energy shocks and shrinking oil/gas reserves add to inflation risk and price pressures across transport, manufacturing, and households; El Niño could further disrupt food supplies. - AI spending fuels demand and offsets some weakness but also introduces financial stability risks if AI investment expectations shift. - IMF maintains 2026 global growth near 3% but inflation projections nudged up due to energy/food costs; outlook remains fragile and uncertain. - Markets will be watching central bank policy paths and energy supply dynamics, with upcoming notes from the Jackson Hole symposium anticipated to influence Fed signals. If you’re tracking Fed rates or geopolitical risk, this underscores: potential for persistent inflation pressure, limited policy maneuvering, and the dual risk of energy price spikes and AI-driven market dynamics.

오늘 스냅샷은 주식(SPY·QQQ)과 비트코인, 금(GLD), 장기·중기 채권(TLT·IEF), 광범위 원자재(DBC·USO·DBB) 등 대다수 핵심 자산군이 HOLD로 정렬돼 있어, 위험자산과 안전자산 어느 쪽에도 명확한 방향성 베팅이 없는 중립 구간임을 보여준다. 반면 천연가스(UNG)와 농산물(DBA)만 매수 신호를 유지하며, 달러 인덱스 프록시(UUP)는 매도 지속 중인데, 이는 달러 약세 기조 속에서 특정 공급 제약 섹터만 별도의 상승 추세를 타고 있음을 시사한다. 최근 2주 이력을 보면 8월 중순 이후 주식·코인·금·원자재 전반이 매수에서 HOLD로 후퇴하면서 위험선호 흐름이 식었고, 채권은 매도→HOLD로 전환돼 안전자산 회피도 완화됐으며, 달러 매도만 일관되게 이어져 왔다. 결과적으로 오늘은 주요 자산군 간 동조화된 '추세 부재' 상태에서, 에너지와 농산물만 독자적 강세를 보이는 비대칭적 패턴이 나타나는 국면으로 읽힌다.

UNG천연가스 (Natural Gas)매수종가 10.41
추천: 매수 **근거:** 1. **기계적 매수 시그널 확정**: 종가(10.41)가 20일 Donchian 채널 상단을 상향 돌파(`20일 상단 돌파 여부: True`)하여 진입 규칙을 충족했습니다. 청산 조건인 트레일링 스탑(9.69) 하향 이탈도 발생하지 않았습니다(`청산 시그널: False`). 시스템 트레이더의 원칙은 '규칙이 시그널을 주면 실행한다'는 것이며, 현재 규칙은 명백히 매수를 지시합니다. 2. **뉴스 팩트 체크 — 펀더멘털 약세장 속 '돌파'의 의미**: 수집된 기사들은 하나같이 **공급 과잉과 가격 하락 압력**을 전하고 있습니다. - **EIA 8월 STEO (EnergyReader.io / Carolina Curiel 요약)**: "역대 최대 생산량(122.5 Bcf/d)과 기록적 재고(10월 말 3,985 Bcf 전망)로 Henry Hub 가격이 내년 초까지 $3 아래에 머무를 것"이라며 **가격 전망치를 하향 조정**했습니다. 생산-수요 갭이 30 Bcf/d 이상 벌어져 구조적 공급 과잉임을 확인시켜 줍니다. - **AGA 8월 마켓 인디케이터**: "미국 내 공급 과잉과 재고 증가로 근월물 가격이 $2.74~$2.81 수준에 머물며, EIA 전망치도 $3.44로 6% 하락"했다고 보도했습니다. - **해석**: 이 뉴스들은 **'왜 그동안 추세가 하락했는지(일목 구음운, 100일 돌파 실패)'를 설명하는 배경 사실**입니다. 하지만 추세추종 시스템은 펀더멘털 '예측'으로 매매하지 않고, **가격 움직임(돌파) 그 자체**에 반응합니다. 악재가 다 반영된 저가권에서 20일 고점 돌파가 나왔다는 것은, 공급 과잉 재료에도 불구하고 매수세가 단기 고점을 넘겼다는 **가격 행동의 변화**를 의미합니다. 이것이 기계적 매수의 유일한 근거이며, 뉴스는 '진입 타이밍이 펀더멘털상 불편한 구간임'을 상기시킬 뿐 판단을 바꾸지 않습니다. 3. **일목균형표(보조 참고) 상충에 따른 리스크 관리**: 현재 주가는 **구름 아래에 있고 음운(하락 구름)**이 형성되어 있어, 중장기 추세 필터(100일 돌파 실패)와 일치하는 **하락 추세 잔재**가 확인됩니다. 기계적 진입 규칙(20일 돌파)과 보조 필터(일목/100일)가 엇갈리는 구간입니다. - **대응**: 정석대로 진입하되, **진입 비중을 표준 단위의 50% 이하로 축소**하여 리스크를 제한합니다. 추가 상승으로 100일 상단 돌파 및 구름대 진입에 성공하면 비중을 늘리고(피라미딩), 실패하여 트레일링 스탑(9.69) 이탈 시 기계적으로 전량 청산합니다.

Natural Gas Market Indicators – August 20, 2026 - American Gas Association
www.aga.org · 2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z

Summary for: natural gas price outlook macro analysis Key takeaways from the August 20, 2026 Natural Gas Market Indicators (AGA): - US market: Well supplied heading into fall shoulder season. Strong production supports demand globally, but a heat dome in the South boosts regional cooling demand and slows storage injections. Henry Hub prices have cooled; EIA’s STEO lowered the 2026 Henry Hub spot price forecast to $3.44/MMBtu (down 6% from July) and the annual forecast is ~20% below February 2026 levels. - Global balance: Tightening LNG market contrasts with bearish US domestic picture. Temporary maintenance at US export terminals (notably Freeport) reduces feedgas demand by ~2 Bcf/d, but is expected to end in late August, re-connecting more US supply to higher European/Asian prices. EU storage is below normal (60.8% full as of Aug 15, below five-year minimum), exerting additional tightness alongside elevated LNG demand from Europe/Asia. - Prices and near-term outlook: Henry Hub remains sub-$3, with September contract averaging around $2.74 from late July; the August 19 settle at $2.81. Market sentiment suggests futures could average about $3.14/MMBtu over the next 12 months (roughly 33 cents above current levels). - U.S. production outlook: Marketing gas production set to hit new annual records in 2026 (about 123 Bcf/d marketed), driven by Permian associated gas and Haynesville growth to meet Gulf Coast feedgas demand. Dry gas production also on track for a new record (~111.2 Bcf/d in 2026; +3.3% vs 2025). - Key questions driving macro outlook: - LNG competition: How will European/Asian buyers respond as EU storage remains tight and LNG cargo competition rises with elevated international prices? - Storage dynamics: Will robust US production accelerate injections into storage as demand softens into fall? - Price trajectory: Will weakening summer demand keep Henry Hub prices subdued, or will winter heating demand provide upward pressure? Bottom line for price outlook: Near-term US prices remain subdued despite rising demand and strong production; the global tightness due to low EU stocks and higher LNG prices supports potential upside risk into winter, but robust US supply and falling near-term prices imply a cautious, mixed macro outlook with volatility tied to LNG flows and storage movements.

Key takeaway for price outlook: - Structural oversupply domestically supports low Henry Hub prices in the near term, conditioned on timely LNG export capacity utilization and slower domestic demand growth. The main price sensitivities are LNG export ramp-up timing and any unexpected demand shifts (notably data-center electricity use).

Citi Elevates Grain Targets as Super El Nino Risk Rises
Brian McColl · 2026-08-25T11:29:48.000Z

Citi’s latest outlook flags elevated risk for agricultural commodities due to a strengthening Super El Niño. Key takeaways: - Price targets raised for corn, soybeans, and wheat (3-month and 12-month horizons): - Corn: 3-month $5.40, 12-month $5.90 per bushel - Soybeans: 3-month $12.75, 12-month $13.25 per bushel - Wheat: 3-month $7.25, 12-month $7.75 per bushel - Core rationale: NOAA’s August 2026 update indicates a very strong El Niño with >90% probability, and a 69% chance it exceeds all events since 1950 in Oct–Dec, implying heightened weather disruption risk to global crops. - Most exposed commodities: palm oil, robusta coffee, rice, sugar, cocoa, and Australian wheat; with concentrated risk in Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and parts of Brazil. - Mechanisms: El Niño-related production risk, potential for lower yields, higher demand for substitutions, and potential for tighter supply dynamics; a higher likelihood of adverse weather impacts is not yet fully priced in. - Supply-demand catalysts reinforcing bullish stance: weaker yields from weather, robust export demand, Black Sea disruptions, fertilizer/energy costs, and rising biofuel demand. - Specific weather/geo risks: heat/drought in Europe affecting wheat; El Niño impacts on palm oil in Indonesia/Malaysia; possible substitution effects boosting soybean oil and soybean prices via crush demand. Bottom line: Citi views the agricultural complex as increasingly vulnerable to El Niño-driven weather shocks, justifying higher price targets across major grains and highlighting notable risk concentration in palm oil, coffee, rice, sugar, cocoa, and Australian wheat. This paints a more cautious, upside-biased market outlook for 2026–2027 amid climate-driven supply uncertainty.

Tariff-free beef imports initially pressured but recovered to close; expect potential strength in winter-beef complex to open higher. Hogs: early weakness followed by a modest rally; possible upside continuation if the market sustains gains. - Treasuries/Interest rate backdrop: Front-end yields rising while long-end yields retreat; post-Treasury dynamics influencing curve positioning. Market eyeing deficit/debt concerns as a risk factor for macro-driven commodity moves. - Coffee and Sugar: December Coffee holding near two-month highs on tight near-term supplies, Brazil quality concerns, and El Nino risks affecting future harvests. October Sugar softer after recent highs, supported by European beet crop concerns and India’s near-term duty-free import policy amid high domestic prices. - Brazil/El Niño risk: Brazilian coffee and sugar markets show vulnerability to El Niño-driven dry spells later in the year, with Brazil’s weather and harvest timing continuing to shape supply expectations. Bottom line: The outlook for agricultural commodities remains sensitive to crop-tour data and demand signals (notably China for soy). Soybeans/meal appear cautiously bullish on supply constraints and demand, while corn shows potential upside from tighter production expectations. Cattle/hogs and energy-linked macro factors add volatility. Vigilance on weather risk (Brazil, India, El Niño impacts) and fiscal/deficit concerns shaping macro moves is warranted.

USDA trims wheat stocks as corn, soybean production forecasts shift  - High Plains Journal
Kylene Scott · 2026-08-21T00:00:00.000Z

Here’s a concise outlook based on the USDA WASDE Aug. 12 update, with a focus on agricultural commodities market implications: - Wheat: U.S. 2026-27 production forecast cut to 1.531 billion bushels (down 5 million from July) due to lower harvested area and yield, especially hard red winter and durum. Ending stocks also trimmed to 717 million bushels (down 22% vs. 2025-26). Season-average price raised to $6.20/bu. Implication: tighter wheat supply supports prices; potential for firmer domestic demand and exports if global supply remains constrained. - Corn: Production forecast up to 16.0 billion bushels (up 13 million from July) but beginning stocks down 75 million to 1.9 billion. With higher exports and modestly lower yield, the corn ending stocks fall to about 1.7 billion bushels (down 137 million from July). Price forecast adjusted to $4.50/bu. Implication: tighter-than-expected stocks despite higher production; lingering support from export demand and global substitution effects. - Rice: Production at 158.4 million cwt (up 5.1 million from July) with higher harvested area offsetting lower yield. Higher supplies, domestic use, and ending stocks; exports unchanged. Implication: modest downward price/upbeat supply signal relative to recent expectations. - Soybeans: Production raised to 4.5 billion bushels (up 44 million from July) on higher harvested area (85.8 million acres) and solid yields (first survey-based yield ~52.7 bu/ac, down 0.3 from July). Ending stocks lifted to 320 million bushels; price forecast remains at $11.40/bu. Soybean crush expected higher at 2.78 billion bushels (+30 million). Soybean meal/oil prices: $310/short ton and $0.70/lb. Exports unchanged. Implication: favorable supply growth supports modest downside price risk, but robust domestic crush and meal/oil demand can sustain firm margins; global demand dynamics (China, Southeast Asia) key in price direction. - Global context: Global soybean production higher with increased crush and slightly higher ending stocks; Ukraine production constraints offset by higher Argentina. For corn, global factors include Ukraine export constraints and broader grain demand. Global oilseed shifts contribute to soybean price volatility. Bottom line for market outlook: - Wheat and soybeans show supply considerations that can support prices, though soybeans face some upside from crush demand and exports. - Corn faces a tighter ending stock picture despite higher production, supporting a constructive price trend relative to the July baseline. - Beefing up demand signals (exports, crush margins) and weather in key growing regions will be pivotal in the near term. If you want, I can tailor this to a specific commodity (wheat, corn, soybeans) or compare to previous WASDE months for trend insights.
